meta.description: Multiple sclerosis keyword clusters projected from the main lexicon (wctglpdemo-data/keyword_lexicon.json, schema 3.7) into the per-indication disease-insights file shape. Drug-cluster variants are hydrated with generic + brand names from registries/drugs.json since the main lexicon strips them out (3.6+ matcher inlines them at regex-build time).

clusters.label: MS trial endpoints (EDSS / ARR / MRI)
clusters.description: The endpoints MS trials use — confirmed disability progression on EDSS, annualized relapse rate, new T2 / gad-enhancing MRI lesions, NEDA.

clusters.label: MS Society / advocacy
clusters.description: National MS Society, MS International Federation, MS Trust, and local chapters — patient education, advocacy, and peer programs.

clusters.label: Depression / anxiety (MS)
clusters.description: Mood disorders are common comorbidities in MS — partly disease-driven (cortical involvement, immune signaling), partly reactive.

clusters.label: PML / opportunistic CNS infection
clusters.description: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy — a rare JC-virus opportunistic infection most associated with natalizumab in JCV-positive patients.

clusters.label: EDSS / disability score
clusters.description: Expanded Disability Status Scale — the 0–10 walking-distance-anchored disability score used in MS trials and clinic.

clusters.label: JC virus antibody status
clusters.description: JCV serostatus — checked before and during natalizumab; positive index raises PML risk and drives DMT decisions.

clusters.label: MRI / lesions
clusters.description: Brain and spinal-cord MRI — T2 lesion burden, gadolinium-enhancing (active) lesions, new vs stable; the standard MS monitoring tool.

clusters.label: Annualized relapse rate (ARR)
clusters.description: The standard relapse-frequency metric used in MS trials and patient-facing data.

clusters.label: Cooling strategies
clusters.description: Cooling vests, ice packs, cold drinks, air conditioning — patient workarounds for heat sensitivity.

clusters.label: Physical / occupational therapy
clusters.description: PT, OT, and speech therapy — the workhorse non-pharm interventions for MS function and mobility.

clusters.label: MS symptom / relapse journal
clusters.description: Logging symptoms, suspected relapses, and treatment response to share with the neurology team.

clusters.label: Invisible disability (MS)
clusters.description: Symptoms — fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, pain — that aren't visible; the disbelief and judgment that follow.

clusters.label: Bladder / bowel dysfunction
clusters.description: Urinary urgency, frequency, retention, incontinence; constipation. Common, embarrassing, and frequently undisclosed.

clusters.label: Cog fog / cognitive dysfunction
clusters.description: Slowed processing speed, working-memory and attention deficits — common but under-reported in MS.

clusters.label: MS fatigue (lassitude)
clusters.description: The MS-specific fatigue — distinct from ordinary tiredness; one of the most disabling and under-treated symptoms.

clusters.label: Heat sensitivity (Uhthoff's)
clusters.description: Uhthoff's phenomenon — symptoms worsen with heat (hot shower, exercise, weather). Drives cooling strategies.

clusters.label: Numbness / tingling (paresthesia)
clusters.description: Sensory disturbances — numbness, pins and needles, burning — often the first MS symptom patients notice.

clusters.label: Optic neuritis / vision changes
clusters.description: Inflammation of the optic nerve — blurred or lost vision, pain with eye movement — often a presenting MS symptom.

clusters.label: MS pain (neuropathic, MS hug)
clusters.description: Neuropathic pain syndromes in MS — trigeminal neuralgia, the "MS hug" (truncal banding), burning extremities.

clusters.label: Disability progression
clusters.description: The accumulating disability arc patients fear — independent of relapses in progressive forms; "PIRA" in trials.

clusters.label: MS relapse / attack
clusters.description: A new neurologic episode lasting >24 hours — the central event in relapsing MS. Patients call them attacks, flares, or exacerbations.

clusters.label: Spasticity / muscle stiffness
clusters.description: Increased muscle tone, spasms, and stiffness — common in lower limbs.

clusters.label: Walking difficulty / gait
clusters.description: Loss of ambulation — slowed walking speed, foot drop, falls, eventual use of cane, walker, or wheelchair.

clusters.label: Multiple sclerosis (diagnosis)
clusters.description: Identification with the diagnosis and its course — relapsing-remitting (RRMS), secondary-progressive (SPMS), primary-progressive (PPMS), clinically isolated syndrome (CIS).

clusters.label: Refractory / failed-everything framing
clusters.description: The "tried everything" arc — DMT failures stack up, motivating openness to CAR-T or autologous stem-cell transplant.

clusters.label: PML / JCV risk concerns
clusters.description: PML risk weighed against natalizumab benefit — JCV positivity, prior immunosuppression, treatment duration.

clusters.label: DMT discontinuation risk
clusters.description: Fear that stopping DMT in older or stable MS will trigger rebound or new disease activity — DISCOMS-type questions.

clusters.label: High-efficacy first vs escalation
clusters.description: The treatment-strategy debate patients hear about — start with high-efficacy DMT vs escalate from platform therapy.

clusters.label: Fingolimod (Gilenya)
clusters.description: First oral DMT for relapsing MS; S1P receptor modulator. First-dose cardiac monitoring required.

clusters.label: Anti-CD20 DMTs (class)
clusters.description: The high-efficacy anti-CD20 class — ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, ublituximab, off-label rituximab — for relapsing and progressive MS.

clusters.label: DMT switching / cycling
clusters.description: The pattern of moving between DMTs over years — switching for breakthrough disease, side effects, or pregnancy planning.

clusters.label: Injectable DMTs (interferons / glatiramer)
clusters.description: Platform injectable DMTs — interferon-beta products (Avonex, Rebif, Betaseron, Plegridy) and glatiramer acetate (Copaxone).

clusters.label: Oral DMTs (fumarates / teriflunomide / cladribine)
clusters.description: The oral disease-modifying therapy options patients name — fumarates (Tecfidera, Vumerity), teriflunomide (Aubagio), cladribine (Mavenclad).

clusters.label: S1P modulators (class)
clusters.description: Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators — fingolimod, siponimod, ozanimod, ponesimod. Oral, lymphocyte-sequestering.

clusters.label: Natalizumab (Tysabri)
clusters.description: Alpha-4 integrin antagonist for relapsing MS; IV every 4 weeks via TOUCH program. High efficacy offset by PML risk in JCV-positive patients.

clusters.label: Ocrelizumab (Ocrevus)
clusters.description: Anti-CD20 B-cell-depleting antibody approved for relapsing and primary progressive MS; 600 mg IV every 6 months.

clusters.label: Ofatumumab (Kesimpta)
clusters.description: Anti-CD20 antibody for relapsing MS; subcutaneous self-injection monthly. Same class as ocrelizumab but home-administered.

clusters.label: Ublituximab (Briumvi)
clusters.description: Glycoengineered anti-CD20 antibody for relapsing MS; ~1-hour infusion every 6 months.

clusters.label: DMT side effects (injection / flushing / labs)
clusters.description: Common DMT side effects patients name — injection-site reactions, fumarate flushing, GI upset, lymphopenia, fatigue.

clusters.label: Infusion reactions
clusters.description: Infusion-related reactions to anti-CD20 DMTs — itching, throat tightness, fevers — usually with the first dose.

clusters.label: Quality of life (MS)
clusters.description: Felt impact of MS and DMTs on daily life — stamina, function, independence, "stop the progression," "back to myself."
